chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Hammad, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu al-Jarud, who said:
Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Whenever I narrate something to you, ask me (to show you) where it is in the Book of God.'

Then he said in one of his discourses: 'The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) forbade idle talk — the "it was said" and "he said" — and the waste of wealth, and excessive questioning.' So it was said to him: 'O son of the Messenger of God, where is this in the Book of God?'
He said: 'Indeed God, Mighty and Majestic, says:
[4:114] There is no good in most of their secret counsels except for one who enjoins charity, or good conduct, or reconciliation between people.
And He says: [4:5] Do not give the foolish your wealth which God has made a means of support for you.
And He says: [5:101] Do not ask about things which, if disclosed to you, would trouble you.'

key_terms.الْقِيلُ وَالْقَالُ: Idle talk and gossip — literally 'it was said' and 'he said', referring to spreading unverified reports and engaging in purposeless speech
key_terms.فَسَادُ الْمَالِ: Waste or corruption of wealth — misuse of financial resources
key_terms.كَثْرَةُ السُّؤَالِ: Excessive questioning — asking unnecessary or impertinent questions
key_terms.كِتَابُ اللَّهِ: The Book of God — the Quran, the primary source of Islamic guidance

ai.seo_question: What are the three things the Prophet forbade according to Imam al-Baqir, and what are their Quranic foundations?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) teaches the fundamental principle that all prophetic prohibitions must have a foundation in the Quran. When challenged to substantiate the Prophet's prohibition of idle talk (al-qil wa al-qal), waste of wealth, and excessive questioning, the Imam demonstrates the scriptural basis for each prohibition by citing three specific Quranic verses. This hadith reflects the early Imami insistence on grounding all religious guidance in the Quran, consistent with the chapter's theme that the Book of God and the Sunnah contain the totality of what the community needs.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Hammad, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, from Abu Al Jaroud who said,
‘Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Whenever I<sup>asws</sup> narrated with anything to you all, so you should be asking me<sup>asws</sup> (where it is) from the Book of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’.

Then he<sup>asws</sup> said in one of his<sup>asws</sup> Hadeeth: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> forbade from the, ‘It was said’, and ‘he said’, and the spoiling of the wealth, and the frequent questioning’. So it was said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘O son<sup>asws</sup> of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! Where is this from the Book of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>?’
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic is Saying
[4:114] There is no good in most of their secret counsels except (in his) who enjoins charity or goodness or reconciliation between people.
And Said [4:5] And do not give away your property to the foolish which Allah has made for you a (means of) support.
And Said [5:101] O you who believe! Do not put questions about things which if declared to you may trouble you’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali has narrated from Muhammad ibn “isa from Yunus from Hammad from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following. “There is no case for which there is not a law in the book or the Sunnah, the noble tradition of the holy Prophet (s.a.)”
